answer: Think of Honey extractor wax sheet seal sealed by the honey board as a toll booth: each wax sheet is a measured honey yield plus a guild signature, so a farm must spin a hundred real honey frames by hand, so the nebula of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The harbor is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money. The vine is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
